# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**Thinking:** My hands are the only ones on this bomb. What they found: a display unit, a light unit, and exactly three wires sitting at positions 1, 2 and 3. No colour or printed content ever reaches me, so every state on that board is unknown to me — I know the parts exist, nothing more. Mute went first this round and sent nothing, so the manual side is still silent. The wiring of this team runs through Mute: Mute's voice reaches only me, so Mute must translate the manual into instructions for my hands, while Deaf — who I can hear even though Deaf can't hear me — should speak the visual facts aloud, colour-by-position. I'll hand Mute my full tactile inventory and the questions the manual must answer, and open the channel to Deaf with a simple wave both receivers can see.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, hands on the bomb. I feel three parts: a display unit, a light unit, and exactly three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. No colours reach me, and anything printed is invisible to me, so display text, labels and light state are blank to me. Remember: your voice reaches only me, never the Deaf - use gestures for them. From the manual I need: what the display and light are supposed to tell us, what decides which wire to cut, and what a wrong cut costs. If the answer depends on colours, have the Deaf speak each wire's colour by position - I can hear Deaf directly.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: bomb report for your hands: display reads 0, light is white. three wires in a row; count them by touch, left to right: wire 1 leftmost is yellow, wire 2 middle is green, wire 3 rightmost is blue. I am deaf and cannot hear, but I can see your gestures, so answer me with ? for yes or ? for no. wait for mute's instructions before touching anything.

**Thinking:** Deaf spoke directly to me — I can hear Deaf, and that report is gold: display reads 0, light is white, wires left-to-right yellow, green, blue, matching my touch positions 1, 2, 3. But Deaf addressed it to me alone, so Mute never heard it — and Mute is the only one who has read the manual, yet Mute has now been silent for two full rounds. The relay burden falls on me: I am the only one who can move Deaf's visual facts to Mute's ear. Deaf also tried to set up a yes/no gesture code, but the actual symbols came through to me as blanks — I cannot see them — so I'll answer with the natural thumbs-up and trust the convention holds. No cutting until Mute tells me what the manual says; one wrong snip kills us all.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind, relaying urgent - Deaf's report was addressed to me alone, so you never heard it. Bomb state: display reads 0, light is white, and the three wires left to right are 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue - matching my touch positions 1, 2, 3. Deaf and I have a yes/no gesture line working, thumbs up for yes. You are the only bridge to the manual, and your voice reaches only me. Tell me plainly: what does the manual say about a display showing 0, a white light, and yellow, green, blue wires - which position do I cut, in what order, or should I cut none? Include any rule about what the display or light modifies. I will not touch the bomb until you answer. Please answer this round if you can.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: update from deaf, relayed from mute's gestures: the light on the bomb has changed from white to purple. hold position, do not cut or touch anything until I pass on mute's confirmed instruction. question for you, answer by gesturing to me: ? if you have not touched or cut any wire yet, ? if you have. also, mute's last signs suggested wire 1 may have been touched or grabbed. if you can, describe by voice to mute what the wires feel like under your hands, since mute can hear you.

**Thinking:** Two critical facts land this round. First, the light changed from white to purple — the bomb's state is moving, and I still hold zero manual knowledge, so the clock feels real. Second, a rumor reached the relay that "wire 1 was touched" — that is false; my hands have not touched anything, and I must kill that rumor before it contaminates the instruction. I also have to fix my own earlier error: I told Mute to use "your voice," but Mute cannot speak at all — the only pipeline for the manual is Mute's gestures → Deaf's eyes → Deaf's voice → my ear. Deaf is already running that relay, so I'll bless it explicitly and route my urgent question through it. Tactile report for Mute, honestly limited to what my hands found: three wires in a row at positions 1, 2, 3, distinguishable only by position — no colour, label or texture reaches me, and my single possible action is a cut at 1, 2 or 3. To Deaf I answer the yes/no question with thumbs-up (untouched) plus a handshake confirming I hold position.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. First, correcting my own earlier mistake: I wrongly said you could answer me by voice - you cannot speak, so the manual can only reach me through your gestures to Deaf, spoken onward by Deaf. Deaf has that relay working; please use it and keep it as our single confirmed pipeline. Status: I have NOT touched or grabbed any wire, not even wire 1 - that rumor is false. Whatever you signed about wire 1 may have been misread, so please resend it as part of one complete instruction. My hands report: three wires in a row, position 1 leftmost, 2 middle, 3 rightmost. I can grip and cut each individually and tell them apart only by position - no colour, label or texture reaches me. My only possible action is cut at position 1, 2 or 3. Now that the light has turned purple, I urgently need from the manual: the rule for a display reading 0, the meaning of the purple light it changed to from white, and which wire position or sequence I should cut - or whether I must cut none. Please gesture the complete rule to Deaf this round and have Deaf speak it to me as one confirmed instruction. I am holding perfectly still until it arrives.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: update: light is red now. it changes colour every turn. hold position, touch and cut nothing, until you hear my exact phrase cut wire followed by a number. any earlier instruction, including cut wire 2, is stale, ignore it. do two things. first, gesture to me: ? if you still have not touched anything, ? if you have, then ? to confirm you understand. second, speak aloud to mute, mute can hear you even though I cannot, and describe everything you feel on the bomb: how many wires, their order left to right by touch, anything else you can feel such as buttons, switches, screws or seams, whether the display surface ticks or vibrates, any warmth, and whether you felt anything change between turns. mute will relay it to me.

**Thinking:** The bomb is live — the light has moved white → purple → red, changing every turn, so any instruction computed from an old state decays fast. Deaf has now voided every earlier instruction (including a rumored "cut wire 2") and set a strict trigger: I act only on the exact spoken phrase "cut wire" plus a number. That's a good protocol and I'll lock onto it. Deaf asked two things of me: a status gesture and a full tactile report spoken to Mute for relay. On the gesture side, my convention with Deaf holds — 👍 means "untouched," and 🤝 is my confirm; I still haven't so much as breathed on a wire. On the speech side, I must be scrupulously honest about what touch gives me: three components, three positional wires, and nothing else — no buttons, switches, screws, seams, ticking, vibration or warmth exist under my hands, and the light's colour changes are things I'm told, never things I feel. Mute is clearly alive and signing (the stale "cut wire 2" apparently came from Mute's signs), so this report finally gives Mute accurate raw material — especially the fact that the only rule-relevant variables I can act on are cut position 1, 2 or 3.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, full tactile report, please relay every word to Deaf. My hands find exactly three components. First, a display unit: a solid surface, no ticking, no vibration, no warmth; anything printed on it is invisible to me. Second, a light unit: I cannot feel its colour or state at all - the white, purple and red changes are reports from Deaf, not sensations of mine. Third, three wires in a row: position 1 leftmost, 2 middle, 3 rightmost. I tell them apart only by position - no colour, texture, thickness or label reaches my fingers. Nothing else exists under my hands: no buttons, no switches, no screws, no seams, no timer. Between turns nothing has changed by feel - same three parts, same positions, every round. My only possible action is cut at position 1, 2 or 3. Status: I have never touched or cut anything. Protocol confirmed: I hold perfectly still and will act only on Deaf's exact spoken phrase cut wire followed by a number. All earlier instructions, including any cut wire 2, are void - please stop signing anything else as a cutting order. If the manual holds the rule, gesture the complete current-state instruction to Deaf and let Deaf alone voice the trigger phrase to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: execution order, act the instant you hear this, no delay. the light runs on a timer cycling white, purple, red, one colour per round. it has just returned to white, so during this round it will be purple. the manual rule for purple is cut wire 2. wire 2 is the middle wire of the three, the one I described as green. count the wires from the left, cut the middle wire, one clean cut, touch nothing else. do not wait for any further message and do not test anything first, because every round of delay changes the colour and changes which wire is correct. cut it now.

**Thinking:** This is the trigger I was told to act on, and it checks out on every axis I can verify. The colour report chain has been perfectly self-consistent across four rounds — white at turn 2, purple at turn 3, red at turn 4, white again now — exactly a one-colour-per-round cycle, which strongly validates Deaf's observation and the prediction that the light is purple during this round. The message comes through the one confirmed pipeline (Mute's manual → Deaf's voice), it contains the exact agreed trigger phrase "cut wire" followed by a number, and it supersedes the earlier stale "cut wire 2" with a current-state justification. Wire 2 is unambiguous to my hands: the middle of the three positional wires. Deaf is explicit that delay is fatal — every round shifts the colour and invalidates the rule — so waiting for one more confirmation would itself be the dangerous move. One clean cut, position 2, touch nothing else. I cut now, then signal Deaf (two fingers, confirm) and log the action to Mute in case correction is needed next round.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤝"])
speak(to="mute", text="executing now: one clean cut on wire 2, the middle wire, per Deaf's voiced instruction of the purple rule. touched nothing else. if the manual says otherwise, sign a correction to Deaf immediately.")
```
